groups.title: Server Endpoints
groups.question: A mobile app needs a JSON API from your SvelteKit project. Explain how you would build endpoints that return consistent responses.

followUps.API routes with plus server.ts files: How do +server.ts files create API endpoints?
followUps.json and error helpers for API responses: What do the json() and error() helpers do?

evidence.text: +server.ts exports functions named after HTTP methods.
Each returns a Response object.
They live alongside page routes in the same app.
json() serialises data and sets the right content type.
error() produces an error response with a status code.
Using them gives consistent responses across endpoints.

groups.title: Rendering Strategies
groups.question: Your marketing pages could be static, a dashboard does not need server rendering, and you must deploy to a Node server. Explain the rendering options and adapters.

followUps.SSR, CSR, and prerendering page options: How do ssr and prerender options change how a page is built?

evidence.text: ssr = false renders the page only in the browser.
prerender = true builds the page as static HTML at build time.
Static pages are fastest and good for SEO; browser-only pages lose server-rendered content.
An adapter turns the build into the format a platform needs.
adapter-node produces a Node.js server.
adapter-static outputs a fully static site.

groups.title: Environment and Config
groups.question: A developer imported a secret API key into a component, and builds behave differently on different hosts. Explain environment variables and SvelteKit configuration.

followUps.Public vs private environment variables: How do private and public environment variables differ in SvelteKit?

evidence.text: $env/static/private is for server-only values.
Public values need the PUBLIC_ prefix and can be used in the browser.
Importing private values into client code would leak them, and SvelteKit blocks it.

notEnough: Only saying there are two kinds.

evidence.text: It sets the adapter for the target platform.
It defines path aliases.
It holds SvelteKit options that affect how the app builds.

groups.title: Path Aliases and Module Resolution
groups.question: Your imports are full of ../../../ paths and someone accidentally imported database code into a component. Explain $lib and server-only modules.

followUps.Server-only modules with plus server res: How does $lib/server stop secrets reaching the browser?

evidence.text: $lib points to src/lib.
It replaces long relative imports.
It is the standard place for shared components and utilities.

notEnough: Only saying it is an alias.

evidence.text: Modules in $lib/server can only be imported by server code.
Importing them from client code fails the build.
This keeps database code and secrets out of the browser bundle.

notEnough: Only saying it is for server code.
